what: The big section name sits one line up, lying slanted with skewY(-20°) (left origin), hidden outside the wrapping cell. Once the top edge of that slanted box rises 200px above the bottom of the screen, it comes down over 1s ease-in-out and stands straight — only once.

options.offset: How many px above the screen’s bottom edge it triggers when lifted, default 200
options.ease: Curve — a css name or bezier numbers like “0.42,0,0.58,1”, default ease-in-out
options.y: Vertical offset of the hidden position — px number or CSS length, default -100% (one line up). 30 means 30px down
options.fade: 1 means transparent while hidden, then turns on with the same length and curve, default off
options.origin: Tilt axis (css transform-origin), default left — STUDIO type is top left

note: The parent must be wrapped in overflow: hidden so the title starts hidden (original .t-enjoy__title-box etc.). If the title is inline-block, the tilted box width equals the text width, so it stands at the same time as the original · STUDIO appear type (window-hero-stacked-services): y: 30; skew: 30; fade: 1; origin: top left; dur: .8; ease: 0.22,1,0.36,1; offset: 0. The original uses IntersectionObserver (threshold 0), so it triggers as soon as the box touches the bottom edge of the screen

from.where: index.html big headings for ENJOY·FAQ·ACCESS·NEWS·BOOK NOW (original .text-animation → .text-animation__move, common_top.js offset 200)

index.html, about.html etc. Latin section names (Services·Shop·Award Program·Project Story·Partner·News·Media·Recruit, service names): original STUDIO .appear (opacity 0 · skew(0,30deg) · translate 0 30px → 800ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), wrapping cell overflow clip)
